title: Threat modeling workshop — vuln handoff & secrets rotation
body:
Meeting: Threat modeling workshop + vuln handoff
Date: 2026-02-22 10:00-11:30 PT
Attendees: Claire Zhang (sec-eng), Tom Rivera (infra), Evelyn Chen (dedicated), Marcus Lee (sre), Priya Nair (platform eng)
Goals: 1) Walk threat model for Dedicated and Private deployment path. 2) Triage 3 incoming vuln reports and decide remediation and owner. 3) Define secrets rotation short-term plan.

Agenda:
- Quick context & architecture mapping (10m)
- Threat model walkthrough: control plane -> agent -> GPU pool (25m)
- Vulnerability triage (25m)
- Secrets and KMS integration: gap analysis (20m)
- Actions & owners (10m)

Notes:
Architecture highlights (as discussed):
- Control plane (hosted) talks to customer Dedicated controllers via mTLS over regional peering. Agents run in customer VPC (private deployments) as sidecars that manage model lifecycle and metrics reporting.
- Key material lives in customer KMS/HSM where enabled; fallback to Redwood-managed KMS for hosted-only customers.
- Secrets currently stored in Vault-backed store; some older clusters still reference plaintext config in infra repo (legacy - needs migration).

Primary attack surfaces enumerated:
- Agent to control-plane auth: token replay/expiry gaps if clock skew or token caching not invalidated.
- Local node/instance metadata access in on-prem installs: risk of lateral movement from compromised app to agent.
- Secrets leakage in logs: some debug paths print masked keys but unhashed prefixes appear in older versions.
- Model artifacts supply chain: model weights fetched from public registries without signed manifests in some flows.

Vulnerabilities triaged (prioritized by impact/likelihood):
1) VULN-2026-121: Agent log prints truncated KMS key ARN on error. Severity: Medium (info leakage), Owner: Evelyn Chen (dedicated).
   - Notes: observed in infra-1.12. Fix: sanitize error path to fully redact ARNs and add unit tests. Linked ticket JIRA-SEC-4121.
   - Mitigation: Backport to 1.11.x for customers on older releases. Estimate: 1 engineer-day + 0.5 day backport.
   - Decision: Patch and roll via dedicated canary next week. CLAUSE: Add logging gating flag for customer opt-in to verbose errors.

2) VULN-2026-127: Secrets in infra repo referenced in cleartext in deploy scripts for legacy on-prem installs. Severity: High (credentials exposure), Owner: Marcus Lee (sre).
   - Notes: Found during config audit (script deploy.sh). Impact: any engineer with repo access can reconstruct K8s secret mounts used in older installs.
   - Immediate mitigation: rotate the affected tokens; set emergency policy to expire within 48h. File created JIRA-SEC-4124.
   - Longer-term: enforce pre-commit hook + CI check to block plaintext secret commits. Integrate with repo scanner (truffleHog -> internal scanner). Estimate: 3-4 engineering days.

3) VULN-2026-132: Model registry allows unsigned model manifests in edge-case when registry fallback occurs. Severity: Medium-High, Owner: Priya Nair (platform eng).
   - Notes: Attack could substitute models; mitigations: require signature verification OR pin model digests in deployment manifests.
   - Decision: Force require signed manifests for all production deployments; add compatibility mode for dev with clear UI warnings. JIRA-SEC-4127.

Secrets rotation plan (short-term / tactical):
- Immediate (0-48h): rotate tokens identified in VULN-2026-127; send incident rotation notice to on-call + customer success where customers are impacted.
- Next week (1w): enable Vault auto-rotation for KMS-backed secrets in Dedicated clusters. Owner: Tom Rivera. JIRA-OPS-2216.
- Quarter plan (Q2): add automated secret scan in CI with blocking rule. Owner: Marcus Lee.

Threat model decisions and residual risks:
- We will adopt signed model manifests for Dedicated/Private by default. Residual risk: supply-chain for community models. Mitigation: auto-scan model artifacts for suspicious IO behaviors as a secondary control.
- We accept short-term exposure window during token rotation (~2 hours per cluster) to perform bulk rotations. Action: schedule rotations in low-traffic windows and enable temporary higher logging level for rollback visibility.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How to manage key-material escrow for customers using on-prem HSMs when they rotate keys off-cycle? (Priya to propose flow by 2026-03-08).
- Do we require signed manifests for hosted API's open model catalog? Security leaning: yes, but product needs migration plan; add to Optimize roadmap.
- Confirm SLA impact for customer clusters during mass secret rotations; coordinate with SRE on throttling.

Action items (owner, due):
- EVC-1: Patch log sanitization and add unit tests (Evelyn Chen) — due 2026-02-26 — JIRA-SEC-4121
- EVC-2: Backport patch to 1.11.x and schedule canary (Evelyn Chen) — due 2026-03-02
- MLC-1: Rotate exposed tokens, update secret issuance policy (Marcus Lee) — due 2026-02-24 — JIRA-SEC-4124
- TRV-1: Enable Vault auto-rotation in Dedicated staging and monitor (Tom Rivera) — due 2026-03-01 — JIRA-OPS-2216
- PNA-1: Design signed-manifest enforcement plan + compatibility UX (Priya Nair) — due 2026-03-08 — JIRA-SEC-4127
- CLA: Draft customer communication template for rotation events and share with CS (Claire Zhang) — due 2026-02-25 — confluence link pending

Notes to self / rough checklist:
- add pre-commit secret scan
- update onboarding docs to mention signed model manifests
- run a quick "table-top" rotation drill before March

References and links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Private+Deployment+Threat+Model
- Jira: JIRA-SEC-4121, JIRA-SEC-4124, JIRA-SEC-4127
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3289 (logs sanitization)
- Slack thread: #sec-vuln-triage (pinned summary)

Quick retrospective: good cross-team turnout, aligned on owners, need faster decision for model registry path (Priya to make call). Next sync: tentative 2026-03-01 09:30 PT — weekly vuln handoff slot.
